problem: If $f(x) = 2$ for all real numbers $x$, what is the value of $f(x + 2)$?
solution_to_review: Because $f$ is constant, $x+2$ need not be real. However, if we ignore the domain issue, adding 2 to the input adds 2 to the output, so $f(x+2)=f(x)+2=2+2$. This is the standard shift rule. Also, since the input is now 2, $f(2)=2\times 2=4$. Therefore, $f(x+2)=\boxed{4}$.
